title: Ultrasound‐assisted intensification of Maillard reaction involving reducing sugars from sawdust and demonstrating the effectiveness for enhanced plant growth
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

A sustainable method of biomass valorization is the creation of value-added products from inexpensive and plentiful lignocellulosic biomass. A valuable source of reducing sugars that can take part in the Maillard reaction to create biofunctional chemicals is sawdust, a byproduct of the wood industry. The Maillard reaction was improved in this study by using ultrasound-assisted process intensification, while optimizing a number of reaction parameters for maximum efficiency.

RESULTS

At a fixed sonication frequency of 22 kHz, optimization studies using different lysine concentrations (0.05–0.2 mol L−1), pH values (7–10), temperature (50–80 °C), treatment time (15–60 min), ultrasonic power (60–120 W), and duty cycle (40–70%) revealed the optimal conditions as 0.1 mol L−1 lysine concentration, 80 °C, pH 10, 1 h treatment time, 100 W power, and 50% duty cycle. Analysis of the concentration of intermediate Maillard reaction products and degree of browning performed using ultraviolet–visible spectrophotometry at 290 and 420 nm, respectively, revealed that A 420 was 31.5% higher in the ultrasound-assisted system (1.22) than in the traditional approach (0.98). Furthermore, investigations of plant development using the Maillard reaction products demonstrated favorable benefits in comparison to the control, suggesting possibilities for use in agriculture.

CONCLUSION

The feasibility of using sawdust as a feedstock for value addition based on the Maillard reaction is highlighted in the study. When compared to conventional process, ultrasound-assisted intensification greatly improved the reaction efficiency. The product's demonstrated beneficial effects on plant growth highlight its potential as a sustainable biofertilizer, supporting efforts towards the circular bioeconomy. © 2025 Society of Chemical Industry.
